descriptionBody: The Cherry Creek segment extends between the junction of FR 609 and SR 288 and the junction of FR 288 and FR 200 near Young in Gila County. The alignment follows the rugged Cherry Creek drainage, with the trail alternating between rocky canyon bottoms, narrow two-track climbs, and occasional creek crossings. Vegetation transitions from juniper and piñon pine on the uplands to cottonwood, sycamore, and riparian growth along the creek corridors, with expansive views of the Sierra Ancha highlands to the east.

The creek supported indigenous Salado and Apache settlements, with cliff dwellings and cultural sites still visible in nearby canyons. Today, the route blends rugged scenery with a sense of living history, connecting riders to both natural beauty and Arizona's frontier past.
amenitiesNote: Limited along the alignment itself, but services including food, fuel, lodging, and camping are available in the nearby community of Young, accessible via FR 288. Additional dispersed camping opportunities exist throughout the surrounding Tonto National Forest.
safetyNote: This is a remote and rugged segment that requires high-clearance 4WD. Seasonal rains can make the Cherry Creek crossings hazardous or impassable, and summer heat in lower elevations can be extreme. If Cherry Creek is impassable, riders can travel between trail segments by following FR 288 through Young. Riders should carry extra water, fuel, and navigation tools before attempting this section.
pointsOfInterest: Scenic pullouts along FR 288 (Desert to Tall Pines Scenic Road)
Salado and Apache cliff dwellings and cultural sites in nearby canyons
